entities.name: PMID:25424123
observations: Retrospective single-institution cohort of men with biochemical failure after salvage radiotherapy following prostatectomy; median follow-up after salvage radiotherapy was 7.9 years.

At salvage ADT initiation, less advanced disease was defined as PSA doubling time >3 months and no distant metastasis; more advanced disease was PSA doubling time <3 months without metastasis or any distant metastasis.

Compared with less advanced disease, more advanced disease was associated with higher prostate-cancer-specific mortality (HR 2.8, 95% CI 1.4–5.6, p=0.005) and overall mortality (HR 1.9, 95% CI 1.0–3.5, p=0.04).
In a multivariable analysis, PSA doubling time <3 months predicted prostate-cancer-specific mortality (HR 4.2, 95% CI 1.6–11.1) and overall mortality (HR 2.9, 95% CI 1.3–6.7).

entities.name: PMID:26165416
observations: Contextual retrospective cohort of men with biochemical recurrence after salvage radiotherapy; the retrieved evidence reported 10-year overall survival of 59%, prostate-cancer-specific survival of 73%, and metastasis-free survival of 75%.
The retrieved evidence did not provide an adjusted mortality comparison by disease advancement at ADT initiation.

entities.name: Less advanced salvage ADT disease
observations: After biochemical failure following salvage radiotherapy, less advanced disease at salvage ADT initiation was associated with lower subsequent prostate-cancer-specific and overall mortality in a retrospective cohort.
Advancement was measured primarily by pre-ADT PSA doubling time and distant metastasis, not a new clinical T-stage classification.
The association is prognostic and does not establish that earlier ADT initiation itself caused lower mortality; the comparison was nonrandomized.

entities.name: Glycogen storage disease type I
observations: Blocks conversion of glucose-6-phosphate to free glucose, impairing both glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis.
Typical phenotype includes severe fasting intolerance, doll-like facies, protuberant abdomen, hepatomegaly, growth impairment, and hyperlipidemia causing lipemic blood.
GSD Ia is usually caused by biallelic G6PC variants; GSD Ib is caused by SLC37A4 variants and may include neutropenia.

entities.name: G6PC
observations: Encodes the glucose-6-phosphatase catalytic component; biallelic deficiency causes glycogen storage disease type Ia.

entities.name: Glucose-6-phosphate
observations: Accumulates when glucose-6-phosphatase activity is deficient and is diverted into glycogen synthesis and lipogenesis.

entities.name: Fasting hypoglycemia with lipemia
observations: The combination of severe fasting intolerance/hypoglycemia, hepatomegaly, doll-like facies, protuberant abdomen, and milky lipemic blood is characteristic of glycogen storage disease type I.
